title: Your Credit Card Bill Just Got Fairer: No More Interest on Penalties!
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has changed credit card billing rules from August 1, 2026. Banks can no longer charge you interest on unpaid late fees, conven.

faq.q: What is a "finance charge" on a credit card?
faq.a: A finance charge is essentially the interest a bank charges you for borrowing money through your credit card, especially if you don't pay your full bill by the due date.

faq.q: Do I need to do anything for these new rules to apply to my card?
faq.a: No, you don't need to take any specific action. Your credit card issuer is responsible for updating their billing systems to comply with the new RBI framework.

faq.q: How can I check if my bank is following the new rules?
faq.a: You should carefully review your credit card statements issued after August 1, 2026. Look for how interest is calculated and if late fees or taxes are clearly itemised and not attracting additional interest. If something seems off, contact your bank's customer care.

faq.q: Will this affect my credit score?
faq.a: These specific rules primarily affect interest calculation, not your credit score directly. However, consistently paying your dues on time (even if partial) and managing your credit responsibly are key to maintaining a good credit score.
